ch.s: Verses 1–10: “A man lived in Babylon, and his name was Joakim.”; Verses 11–20: “For they were ashamed to declare their lust, what they desired to do with her.”; Verses 21–30: “If you will not, we will testify against you, that a young man was with you; therefore you sent your maids away from you.””; Verses 31–40: “Now Susanna was a very delicate woman, and beautiful to behold.”; Verses 41–50: “Then the assembly believed them, as those who were elders of the people and judges; so they condemned her to death.”; Verses 51–60: “Then Daniel said to them, “Put them far apart from each another, and I will examine them.””; Verses 61–64: “Then they arose against the two elders, for Daniel had convicted them of false testimony out of their own mouth.”. People named: Susanna, Joakim, Daniel, Moses. Places: Babylon, Judah, Canaan.
q: Read verses 1–10. What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 11–20, what do you learn about leadership and kingship?
Read verse 48 slowly. What does it say about God, about people, and about how to live?
What does Susanna’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of judgment in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Susanna?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.a: Let the seriousness of God's judgment move you to examine your ways and to pray for others.
